text:
Pius Suter spent Tuesday night passing two round numbers. His snap shot 37 seconds into the second period tied the game and gave him his 100th career goal, and it also marked his 200th career point. It helped a Blues team that had gone three games without a win (0-2-1) finally get one, a 3-2 result over Detroit at Enterprise Center.

St. Louis led the game for long stretches. Andrew Copp's tip-in with 13 seconds left in the first period gave Detroit a lead the Red Wings had barely earned, since the Blues out-chanced them through the first two periods. Suter answered, Justin Barron's snap shot made it 2-1 two minutes later, and Jimmy Snuggerud's deflection in the third made it 3-1. Snuggerud, drafted 23rd overall in 2022 and a Minnesota collegian two seasons ago, finished with a goal and an assist, and Dylan Holloway put seven shots on goal. Joel Hofer stopped 30 of 32 and was a shade better than the shots he saw (0.82 goals saved above expected, meaning he allowed fewer than an average goalie would on those chances).

Detroit nearly erased it. The Red Wings out-chanced St. Louis 2.20 to 1.02 in expected goals, a measure of shot quality, in the third period, and Moritz Seider's slap shot with 74 seconds left cut the margin to one. That goal came on a 5% chance. Over the full game our numbers gave the Blues a 57% chance to win after replaying every shot, so the result matches the play more than the late push suggests.

For St. Louis, the win ends the slide and avenges a 5-4 win Detroit took on October 31. Detroit is winless in four (0-4-0).
